subject: research/free-buckreal
professional: a referee in nonlinear system identification of power converters (the Aguirre/UFMG grey-box NARX school, IEEE TCAS-I reviewer); first checks: is the data's known static curve (Vo = 4Vd/3 - Vd u/3, Vd = 24 V, CCM) used or tested, is the standard polynomial NARX baseline on this exact dataset compared, is the free-run comparison fair (initial conditions, delay, parameter count), is a static nonlinearity identifiable from a near-binary PRBS input, and does the uncertainty interval mean anything on one 20 ms record

evidence.correctness: Ran it: `python3.13 -m pytest -q tests` 5 passed in 1.4 s; `python3.13 experiments/run.py` in a scratch copy (2 min 28 s) gives a results.txt byte-identical to the committed one. Recomputed independently in my own script (scratchpad/buckreal/indep.py, no import of buckreal): quantisation step 0.2 V and floor 0.2/sqrt(12) = 0.0577; constant baseline 1.3199 fwd / 1.3191 rev; ARX 1/1, 2/2, 10/10 free-run test 0.617/0.582/0.549 fwd and 0.693/0.819/0.712 rev (equal to results.txt); one-step ARX error 0.12-0.16 V (README 'about 0.13 V'); twin re-simulated with scipy.signal.cont2discrete(zoh)+dlsim from the reported params reproduces 0.7186/0.6159/0.6732/0.5002 exactly once shifted one sample, i.e. lti2 outputs the state after the current input's update (a one-sample lead over strict ZOH; strict-ZOH RMSE 0.707/0.609/0.683/0.511, conclusions unchanged). Steady-state rather than zero initial state moves the Hammerstein test RMSE by <0.006 V, so the headline is robust to that. Not 4: the one-sample lead is undocumented and the headline 'curvature matters' rests on a physically doubtful static fit (see domain).
evidence.completeness: README claims walked: data files and split (1001/999, contiguous, 10 to 20 ms) correct; twin and linear variant, delay chosen on train only, ARX 1/1..10/10, block bootstrap, both directions, results.json params incl. wn ~4870 rad/s (775 Hz), figure script and committed PNG, 5 tests; live page https://marisstella.app/research/free-buckreal/ returns 200 and matches project.json. Every listed table cell matches results.txt. No stubs or TODOs. Runtime stated as 'about 1.5 min', measured 2 min 28 s.
evidence.verification: 5 tests pass (data shape, lti2 DC gain and the textbook overshoot exp(-pi z/sqrt(1-z^2)), ARX recovery of a known system, twin parameter recovery on synthetic data, constant baseline above floor). Seeded 6 mutants with quality_mutate.py: 2 caught (ZOH input matrix doubled; ARX free-run lag index shifted), 4 survived: input delay reversed into an advance (u[delay:]), the linear variant's c2 = 0 removed, bootstrap percentiles 2.5/97.5 -> 25/75, ARX test simulation scaled by 1.02. experiments/run.py (bootstrap, delay selection, the whole comparison) has no test; delay != 0 and structure='linear' are never exercised.
evidence.craft: Read buckreal.py (93 lines), experiments/run.py, figure.py, tests. Small, readable, deterministic (seeded bootstrap), exact ZOH via expm. Defects: lti2 returns the post-update state so output[i] already responds to input[i] (undocumented one-sample lead; the delay grid 0..20 is really -1..19); twin simulation starts from zero state while ARX starts from measured outputs and skips k samples, scored without skip (harmless here, measured); `from scipy.linalg import expm` inside the function; centring constant 2.35 hard-coded twice; block_boot_diff silently drops the last 89 samples (9 blocks of 100 from 989); no requirements file (bare python3 here lacked scipy).
evidence.claims: Checked 9 claims. Backed: every number in the README table and bullets (results.txt), 0.058 V floor, 'nine times' (0.50/0.058 = 8.7), the averages 0.56 vs 0.70, ARX non-monotone in order, wn ~5e3 rad/s in results.json, 5 tests, MIT data licence. Not backed: (1) 'That repository does not say ... what the input scaling is' and 'no component values ... no datasheet to check against': SysIdentPy's own multiobjective tutorial on these exact files (docs/en/user-guide/tutorials/multiobjective-parameter-estimation-overview.md) states the static function Vo = 4Vd/3 - (Vd/3) u with Vd = 24 V (gain -8), and Hafiz, Swain, Mendes, Aguirre (IEEE TCAS-I 2020, arXiv 1909.04320) describe the rig (Vd = 24 V, LM3524 PWM at 33 kHz, PRBS u in 2.2-2.5 V, CCM) citing Aguirre et al. 2000; (2) 'The twin's static curvature matters' presented as physics ('the averaged LC filter behind a duty-to-voltage curve'): the published CCM static law is linear, and the fitted quadratic puts 15.4 V at u = 2.35 against 13.2 V from first principles; (3) 'about 1.5 min' runtime (2.5 min measured).
evidence.fitness: A system-ID researcher could rerun it in minutes and the free-run, swapped-halves, equal-parameter-count design is reusable. But the nearest prior work on this very dataset is not cited or compared: Aguirre, Donoso-Garcia, Santos-Filho (IEEE TCAS-I 47(7), 2000), Correa, Aguirre, Saldanha (TCAS-I 2002), Hafiz et al. (TCAS-I 2020) and the SysIdentPy polynomial-NARX/multiobjective tutorial all identify this converter with the static curve as prior knowledge. My own grey-box check (scratchpad/buckreal/greybox.py) with the published static law fixed and only wn, zeta fitted (2 parameters) gets 0.738 V fwd and 0.489 V rev, i.e. as good as the 5-parameter Hammerstein in reverse (0.500) with no fitted static curve at all, a result the study was one step from and missed. Not new (ARX vs Hammerstein on a tutorial dataset), one record, single session; well below the research brief's programme bar.
evidence.domain: Compared against grey-box NARX practice for this converter (Aguirre 2000; Hafiz 2020) and textbook CCM buck averaging (Vo = D Vd, linear in duty). Sound: free-run scoring, delay chosen on training data, an ARX with equal parameter count, reporting both split directions and the quantisation floor, honest limitations. Departures: (a) the input is near-binary (id: 2.20/2.21 V 456 samples, 2.50/2.51 V 518, only 27 intermediate), so a quadratic static curve is barely identifiable; its 'curvature' is fitted by ~3% transition samples and departs 2.2 V from the known static law at mid-range; (b) the known static law is ignored although it is in the data provider's own docs, and the linear twin's own fit (c1 = -8.02, c0 = 13.39 at 2.35) matches it (-8, 13.2), a validation left unreported; (c) no polynomial NARX baseline, the standard on this dataset; (d) the bootstrap resamples 9 blocks of residuals from fixed fitted models, so it ignores estimation uncertainty and is crude; (e) file sampling_time says 10 us while the source paper reports 1 MHz decimated by 12 (12 us) for its identification data; if the same record, the fitted wn should be scaled by 10/12 (not verifiable from here).

defects.what: Nearest prior work on this exact dataset is uncited and its known static law unused: SysIdentPy's own tutorial on these files gives Vo = 4Vd/3 - Vd u/3 (Vd = 24 V, gain -8) and the Aguirre group's TCAS-I papers (2000, 2002, 2020) identify this converter as grey-box NARX. A 2-parameter twin with that law fixed scores 0.738/0.489 V, matching the 5-parameter Hammerstein in reverse; no polynomial NARX baseline

README says the data's input scaling is unknown and no component values or datasheet exist to check the twin; the static function and Vd = 24 V are published by the data provider, the PWM frequency (33 kHz) and CCM operation in Hafiz et al. 2020

'The twin's static curvature matters' is framed as converter physics, but the CCM static law is linear and the input is near-binary (97% of samples at two levels), so the quadratic is fitted by transition samples and puts 15.4 V at u = 2.35 against 13.2 V from first principles; the gain is not evidence of a physical static nonlinearity

Tests do not cover the experiment or the delay/linear branches: 4 of 6 mutants survive (delay reversed into an advance, linear variant's c2 = 0 removed, bootstrap percentiles changed, ARX test sim scaled)

lti2 returns the state after applying the current input, so output[i] already reacts to input[i]: a one-sample lead over the 'exact zero-order hold' the README states (delay grid effectively -1..19); RMSE shifts by about 0.01 V
Block bootstrap resamples 9 blocks of residuals from fixed fitted models (drops the last 89 samples), ignoring estimation uncertainty; the 'excludes zero' interval is weaker evidence than stated
Runtime stated as 'about 1.5 min'; measured 2 min 28 s
No requirements file for numpy/scipy/matplotlib; bare python3 in the cloud container lacked scipy and the test collection errored

verdict: The numbers are right: the experiment reruns byte-identically, my own ARX, baseline and quantisation recomputations match to three decimals, and an independent scipy ZOH simulation reproduces the twin errors (with an undocumented one-sample lead that does not change any conclusion). It misses the bar on fitness, claims, verification and domain: the data provider's own docs and the Aguirre group's papers give this converter's static law (Vo = 32 - 8u at Vd = 24 V), which the README says is unknown, the 'physics-shaped' Hammerstein fits a quadratic to a near-binary PRBS that departs 2.2 V from that law at mid-range, a 2-parameter twin using the known law matches the 5-parameter one in reverse, no NARX baseline or prior work is cited, and 4 of 6 seeded bugs survive the tests. Finished for what it claims; a TCAS-I referee would send it back for the prior work and the grey-box baseline.
